validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently of GEM. FERC Federal Register Notice of Application, Docket No. CP05-64-000 (filed Feb. 1, 2005; published 70 FR 7724, Feb. 15, 2005) states verbatim: 'FGT proposes to construct a new 17,000 horsepower electric compressor station and approximately 1,600 feet of 18-inch mainline extension. FGT states that the proposed facilities also include a 24-inch Tee and Side Valve on its existing 24-inch turkey point lateral...located in Miami-Dade County, Florida' — this independently names the 'Turkey Point lateral,' gives its diameter (24-inch), and places it at FPL's Turkey Point Power Plant. Separately, EIA's own 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' table (eia-naturalgaspipelineprojects.xlsx, sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)') carries a discrete row: Project Name 'FGT Turkey Point Lateral', Operator 'Florida Gas Trans Co', Project Type 'Lateral', Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2006-12-01, Year In Service 2006, Beg_State/End_State FL/FL, Cost (millions) 19.6, Miles 0.3, Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) 100, Diameter (in) 24, Authority FERC, Docket Number CP05-64. GEM's Length (0.30 mi), Diameter (24 in), Capacity (100 MMcf/d) and StartYear1 (2006) all match this EIA row exactly. CAVEAT ON INDEPENDENCE: both of these sources ultimately trace to the same underlying FERC docket (CP05-64) — the EIA table's own 'Authority/Docket Number' columns cite that docket as its source, and the Federal Register notice is FERC's own restatement of the company's filed application. Per the sweep's independence rule ('FERC + the applicant's own filing IN that FERC docket are ONE origin'), this is closer to one paperwork trail reported via two federal publications than two truly independent investigations. I searched for a third, genuinely separate source — Kinder Morgan's/Energy Transfer's FGT system-map/tariff pages, PHMSA special-permit filings for FGT, the NRC Turkey Point Units 6&7 COL environmental report (which would independently describe the existing gas lateral serving the plant), and general trade press from 2005-2006 — and found none that states these specific figures; the NRC PDFs (nrc.gov/docs/ML1025/ML102580481.pdf and ML1431/ML14311A254.pdf) both 403'd to scripted fetches, and the FGT system map (fgttransfer.energytransfer.com/ipost/FGT/maps/system-map) returns 200 but is a static/interactive map with no extractable text naming the lateral. So EXISTENCE and CLASSIFICATION (it is genuinely an interstate FERC-jurisdictional lateral, not gathering/gas processing) are solid; the numeric SPEC values are corroborated but from what is effectively a single origin. NOTE ALSO: the FERC notice frames the 24-inch lateral as already 'existing' as of Feb. 2005, while the compressor-station/tee project itself (the ~1,600 ft of 18-inch mainline extension) is what completed in Dec. 2006 per EIA — so 'StartYear1 = 2006' most likely marks the in-service date of this compressor/tie-in upgrade project (which EIA books under the lateral's name), not necessarily the very first construction of the 24-inch pipe itself, which may predate 2005. This is a GEM-schema granularity issue (project vs. original construction), not an existence/duplicate problem — no other roster PID represents an earlier 'Turkey Point Lateral' segment, so there is nothing to merge or split against. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as an interstate transmission lateral (NGA section 7 jurisdictional), not a gathering line. DUPLICATE: checked against all 49 other roster rows — no other PID has this length/diameter/capacity combination or documents the same Miami-Dade/Turkey Point location; not a duplicate. SegmentCost DISCREPANCY: EIA's $19.6 million does not match the sheet's $19,400,000 — close (about 1%) but not an exact match, so I am not staging it as a confirming ref; flagged above for Baird's review rather than silently passed.
